item.title: TMS Pie and Butter Braid Fundraiser Sale
item.description:
Talawanda Middle School PTG is holding a pie and butter braid sale from October 15 - November 2 to help students fund class field trips to Glen Helen (7th grade) and Washington, D.C. (8th grade). Students earn 50% profit on pies ($18 each, $22 for pecan) and $6 profit per butter braid ($18 each). Pie pickup is November 18 at 2:30 PM in the TMS Cafe. Order forms and flyers available on Peachtree. Participation is voluntary; profits go into student accounts for school-sponsored trips.

item.title: TMS Citizenship Essay Contest Details
item.description:
TMS is hosting a Citizenship Essay Contest with the theme "If we stop remembering" about what could be lost if we stop sharing veterans' stories. Students may submit essays, letters, poems, or songs in size 14 Times New Roman font, 1.5 spacing, printed and turned in to the TMS Office or Mr. Brinck (room 302) by October 30, 2026. Winners receive $50 in their travel account and top entries will be read at the THS Veterans Day breakfast on November 11 at 8am. All entries will be mailed to local VFW halls for veterans to read. Contact: brinckj@talawanda.org

item.title: Understanding the Green Slip System
item.description:
A Green Slip is issued when a student misses an assignment due date. The student's name is added to a school-wide list and the office calls home. Students should complete the work ASAP and can attend extra help sessions on Tuesdays and Thursdays until 3:30 PM. If missing work is not turned in after attending a help session, the grade becomes a zero and the work is no longer accepted.

item.title: Health Education Curriculum Update Information
item.description:
The district is implementing Senate Bill 288 (Erin's Law) requirements for updated health education curricula covering sexual abuse and violence prevention (K-12). Instruction occurs October 12-26, 2026. Families can review grade-level curriculum materials online and opt students out if desired. Topics include social inclusion, dating violence/healthy relationships, and suicide prevention. Contact your student's school counselor with questions.
